newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't may liberalize pension rules - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't may liberalize pension rules - paper.

text.p: The Brazilian government is considering changes in investment rules for state-owned and private pension fund managers, Gazeta Mercantil financial newspaper reported.
The possible changes to existing regulations will be discussed at the next meeting of the National Monetary Council (CMN), slated for the end of September, the paper said.

Any changes would come after negotiations between the government and the Brazilian Association of Private Pension Funds (Abrapp) and would likely allow fund managers to invest in a broader range of assets and financial instruments, it said.
Brazil has 230 private pension fund managers and 120 funds managed by state companies, with total assets of $65.5 billion, or 11 percent of the country's gross domestic product, it said.
